main_issue: Whether and how Agent D's wake setup at the void deck can be adjusted to accommodate A's mother's wheelchair access, B's daytime sleep, and C's morning exercise group.

A-B.evidence: A and B never address each other; both raise separate concerns to D and both end accepting D's accommodations (turns 25, 28 and 23).

A-C.evidence: A and C never address each other; each raises a separate concern and both end satisfied with D's arrangement (turns 21, 25).

A-D.evidence: D agrees at once to shift the tent (turn 2); A confirms the space is perfect (turns 24-25, 28).

B-C.evidence: B builds on C's mention of the playground area (turn 11), but C says the tent would still be in their spot at 7 a.m. (turn 14); B then drops the move (turn 16) and both accept the final arrangement.

B-D.evidence: B pushes to move the setup (turns 11, 13), D refuses (turns 12, 15); B concedes (turn 16) and D agrees to point the speakers away (turn 17); B thanks D (turn 23).

C-D.evidence: C objects that the tent is in their exercise spot (turn 7) and D asks where they exercise (turn 8); C then offers to use the open area and start at 6:30 (turn 19), and D accepts gratefully (turn 20).
